clue.text: Meagre boxes, last in store, not used to hold sulphur

annotationWithheld.why: Meagre boxes, last in store, not used to hold sulphur (6): holds two complete wordplays, SPARS (boxes) + E (last in store) and SPARE (not used) holding S (sulphur); whichever parse is written, the other's words are left with no job
annotationWithheld.clue: Meagre boxes, last in store, not used to hold sulphur

clue.text: Superficially read periodical beginning to cut corners

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly and superficially

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter of periodical

explanation.surface: Skimming a magazine is the first step to cutting corners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes the P of 'periodical'.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise excessively, spending or doing less than needed, is to scrimp or cut corners.

clue.text: State region not the last in song

indicators.note: in places the shortened region inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: not the last removes the final letter of the region word

parts.note: a zone is a region

explanation.surface: A state's territory is missing from the last verse of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'State'; 'region not the last' is a trimmed synonym rather than the last region of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A south-western US state with Phoenix as its capital is one of the fifty states.

clue.text: Small, small, small lad

parts.note: these two repeats make the first word occur three times, so they tell us the S is tripling

explanation.surface: A very small young boy described with heavy emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a picture: the abbreviated word appears three times, which reads as S tripling, run together into one word for a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth not yet fully grown, a young man, is a lad.

clue.text: Play in backyard with left foot

indicators.note: the play is placed inside the turned-round yard abbreviation

parts.note: YD is the abbreviation for yard, and back turns it round to DY
a play is made up of acts, so an act stands for it

explanation.surface: A child acts out a game in the back garden, leading with the left foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backyard' is split in two: yard abbreviates to YD and 'back' turns it round, so the single word gives the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic metre a foot of one long syllable then two short ones is called by this name.

clue.text: Porter right on the ball

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A railway porter is quite right and on top of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is the dark beer, not the luggage carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick to notice and respond is being watchful and sharp.

clue.text: Symposium presented by a Greek character in 10

indicators.note: in places the letter and character inside the number

parts.note: the figure 10 written as a word
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A conference given by a Greek figure in the tenth entry.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 down, but here it is simply the number written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal conference or series of lectures for discussion on a topic is a forum of this kind.

clue.text: Seafood is possibly gelatinous without one

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of gelatinous may be rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A seafood dish might be jelly-like without its usual ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I (one) out of GELATINOUS ('without') and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny lobster or crawfish is a crustacean eaten as seafood.

clue.text: I arrive for recreation in holiday area

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation: the letters of I arrive are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller announces arriving somewhere for a bit of leisure on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for recreation' rearranges the letters of I ARRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean coast is a famous holiday region, and the word is used for any such coastal resort strip.

clue.text: Salesman is not to put on new coat

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
ain't is the colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A salesman declines the job of painting something afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a fresh coat of paint to a surface means painting it once more.

clue.text: The French score one more in game

parts.note: vingt is French for twenty, a score
et un is French for and one, one added

explanation.surface: French players clock up another point in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty plus one in French is the card game also known as twenty-one or pontoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game in which players aim for a total of twenty-one, similar to blackjack.

clue.text: Range put on patio? Not entirely

indicators.note: to range is to arrange or set in order, so the letters of put on patio are set out differently

explanation.surface: Should a cooking range be put out on the patio?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a cooker but is a verb, arranging the letters of PUT ON PATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly or to a limited extent, i.e. not wholly.

clue.text: Catch villainous captain

definitions.meaning: a barbed fishing implement that catches fish, or to catch as a verb
Captain ... is the pirate villain of Peter Pan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a catching barb and is the name of the pirate captain in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Secret police almost making arrest

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: stasis is a state of arrest, a halting of movement or development

explanation.surface: The secret police are on the point of arresting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of STASIS, a stopping or arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the notorious state security force of communist East Germany.

clue.text: Astronomical eyepiece best in class?

parts.note: astronomy studies the stars, so astronomical suggests star
read as eye piece: the pupil is part of the eye

explanation.surface: An astronomical eyepiece is top of the range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyepiece' reads as a telescope part but splits into eye + piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The top performer among schoolchildren in a class is the outstanding scholar.

clue.text: African individual going to borders of Sierra Leone after talk

indicators.note: after places the individual and the borders behind the talk

parts.note: gab is chatty talk
one is a single individual

indicators.note: borders are the outside letters, here the first and last of the place name

explanation.surface: An African person heads for the frontiers of Sierra Leone after a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' takes the outer letters S and E of 'Sierra Leone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or citizen of Gabon, a west-central African country, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Bugging two items of personal adornment

parts.note: a badge is worn as adornment
a ring is worn on the finger as adornment

explanation.surface: Wearing a brooch and a ring as a means of electronic surveillance.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestering someone persistently is to nag or annoy them.

clue.text: Deliver a forceful speech and hear a gun going off

indicators.note: a gun going off explodes, so the letters of hear a gun are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone startled by gunfire nearby launches into a fierce tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges HEAR A GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant at length and loudly at an audience is to deliver a forceful speech.

clue.text: Put on trial, we hear, when a monarch's on the throne

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of a phrase gives the spelling

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; while a monarch sits on the throne, that period is the monarch's reign

explanation.surface: Someone is prosecuted, rumour has it, during a royal's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns the phrase A REIGN into a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone before a court to answer a charge is to indict them.

clue.text: Western city to avoid

definitions.meaning: ... City, Kansas, a frontier town familiar from cowboy films

explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City is the frontier town of many Westerns, and to evade something is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Display odd bits of iron in play

indicators.note: in places the chosen letters inside the play

parts.note: a drama is a play

indicators.note: odd bits are the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A theatre production shows strange pieces of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes I and O from 'iron', placed in DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic model or museum tableau is a display showing a three-dimensional scene.

clue.text: Reject extremely deficient incentive

indicators.note: deficient at the extreme end means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: to spurn is to reject scornfully

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a stimulus that is badly lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely deficient' cuts the last letter N from SPURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's goad, and so anything that urges one on, is a stimulus or motive.

clue.text: Oh! No bus due when going out — having to stay at home

indicators.note: going out suggests things in disarray, so the letters of oh no bus due are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frustrated commuter finds no bus due and is stuck at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when going out' rearranges OH NO BUS DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to leave their home, through illness or circumstance, is confined there.

clue.text: This is why receiver has new top

indicators.note: the first letter of the receiver word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A radio receiver has a new casing, which explains things.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is criminal slang for a receiver of stolen goods; 'has new top' swaps its F for H, a letter the clue leaves unspecified.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means for this reason or therefore.

clue.text: Time for headless man to appear?

indicators.note: headless means the opening letter is cut off

parts.note: a knight is a chessman

explanation.surface: Darkness is when a headless ghost might appear.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess piece is a man; 'headless' removes K from KNIGHT, whose silent K makes the cut neat.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn are a period of time.

clue.text: Work is not about making choices

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: about signals the letters of is not are moved around

explanation.surface: Doing nothing is not a way of making decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the crossword's usual work; 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternatives available to select from are the possibilities one has to choose.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman cloaked by a local government official at first

parts.note: to cloak something is to hide it, so cloaked means hid
LG is the abbreviation for local government

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman is covered up by a council officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the O of 'official'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the lower Spanish nobility, a minor gentleman, bears this title.

clue.text: Bird allowed outside hostelry

indicators.note: outside means the allowed word surrounds the hostelry

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: A bird is permitted to perch outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Hostelry is an old-fashioned word for a pub or inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown finch noted for its song is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Horrified scallywag has tuna sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase sandwiches the answer between its other letters, hiding it inside

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled that a rascal has tuna sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like lunch but is the hiding signal, enclosing the run within 'scallywag has tuna'.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with horror or shock, someone is appalled.
